subject: On-prem hosting qualification — network/residency constraints & next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@siteminder.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem hosting qualification — network/residency constraints & next steps

Hi Laura — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from Redwood so we’re aligned and can move the tech workstream forward: 

High-level pain points you called out
- Data residency: primary requirement is EU-only storage and processing for all PII and derived model artifacts.
- Air-gap requirement for staging: a physically isolated environment (no outbound internet) for PII test cases.
- Procurement/security: customer-managed KMS/HSM, attestation around supply chain and hardware, and SOC2 evidence requested.
- Network: restricted outbound egress, deep packet inspection in-line, and a narrow maintenance window for upgrades.

Goals we discussed
- Pilot an on-prem inference instance in Q3 (goal: 90-day pilot).
- Achieve 100ms tail latency target for the 95th percentile for the core inference path under expected load (we’ll validate with a load profile).
- Minimal operational footprint for your infra team — Redwood to own runtime ops within agreed boundaries.

Immediate next steps (action owners in parens)
1) Redwood to send: initial network diagram + explicit port/IP allowlist, a short table of KMS/HSM options we support, and an LOE estimate (Evelyn/Karthik) — target EOD Wednesday.
2) SiteMinder to share: existing firewall policy/export and any SOC2/ISO artifacts you can share for our security review (Laura/Ops) — ideally within the week.
3) Schedule: tech deep-dive for the ops/networking team — propose 60 minutes the week of Mar 15. I’ll include a short agenda and a checklist for the session.

Notes/clarifications
- On air-gap: we discussed a pull-based model for model updates (signed bundles over a controlled channel) — Redwood supports this pattern; we’ll outline the mechanics in the network diagram.
- For KMS: we support both customer-managed keys (via KMS) and on-device HSM-backed keys for on-prem deployments; we’ll call out trade-offs.

Attachments: references below to the items we’ll send.

If that matches your notes, I’ll send the network diagram and requirements table by EOD Wednesday and follow up with a Doodle for the deep-dive.

Thanks — talk soon.

Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@siteminder.com>

Cc: ops_team@siteminder.com
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem hosting qualification — network/residency constraints & next steps

Thanks, Evelyn — that summary is accurate. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- We’ll attach our current network policy export (see attached siteminder-network-policy.pdf) — it includes the DPI rules and our proxy/SSL inspection notes.
- The air-gap requirement is non-negotiable for our staging environment; we will want to see the exact pull/update process documented and a signature/verification mechanism on bundles.
- KMS: we prefer to use our existing cloud KMS where possible (customer-managed keys). On-device HSM is acceptable but increases procurement complexity — flagging as a risk.

Ops contact: ops_team@siteminder.com will coordinate on firewall exports and scheduling. They’ll also want to confirm whether Redwood needs temporary egress for validation tests (we can allow a short window with a strict allowlist).

We’d also like to confirm that Redwood can provide an initial LOE for running the pilot in a controlled environment (including monitoring and fallback procedures) — this will help our procurement team.

Laura Chen
Head of Infrastructure
SiteMinder
laura.chen@siteminder.com
(UK office: +44 20 7946 0000)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@siteminder.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem hosting qualification — network/residency constraints & next steps

Hi Laura — thanks for the fast turnaround and for sharing the policy export. A few technical notes and how Redwood proposes to proceed: 

1) Network approach (proposed) - Edge gateway pattern: a small, customer-run gateway VM that handles local inference traffic and enforces egress rules. Model bundles are pulled by the gateway over an allowed, signed channel during scheduled maintenance windows.
- Ports/IPs: to support the pattern we’ll need temporary outbound to these IPs: 52.11.33.210/32, 52.11.33.211/32 (we’ll provide a signed cert pin and short-lived tokens for pull).
- DPI/SSL inspection: our pull uses TLS with certificate pinning; if your proxy performs SSL inspection, you’ll need to whitelist the gateway endpoints or provide a bypass for the pinned connection.

2) Air-gap support
- We support offline bundle delivery and signed bundle verification locally (no long-lived outbound connections required). The gateway validates bundle signatures against your public key (we’ll document the sequence).

3) KMS/HSM
- Customer-managed cloud KMS (recommended) — Redwood can integrate with standard KMS providers for key wrapping. On-device HSM is supported for FIPS/attested flows; we’ll call out procurement impact in the LOE.

4) LOE & next steps
- Deliverables we’ll send by EOD Wed: redwood_onprem_network_diagram_v1.pdf, and a requirements matrix (redwood_onprem_requirements_table.xlsx) with fields for ports, sample maintenance window, and recommended telemetry.
- Proposed tech deep-dive: Mar 16, 10:00–11:00 (US-PST) — agenda: (1) review diagram & allowlist, (2) walk through bundle signing flow, (3) ops validation/port test plan. Confirm if the time works for your Ops team and we’ll send a calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abcdefg123456

Action items for SiteMinder
- Provide a short list of contacts for networking (we have ops_team@siteminder.com) and confirm the allowed maintenance window for outbound pulls.
- Share any additional compliance artifacts beyond SOC2 that you think are relevant (e.g., encryption attestations).

We’ll include a short port-check script with the diagram so your NetOps team can run a quick validation before the deep-dive.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, On-prem
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
